name: Findings from the end-to-end run of the cross-round work
description:
On 29–30 September we ran the whole tool end to end on a local branch: master plus every PR still open around the rerun work (#71, #72, #77, #78, #80). It ran the way a reviewer and an admin use it: repositories discovered and watched, 21 test pull requests on GitHub, 47 review rounds, and every round driven through the console (claim, edit, release, partner replies, closing proposals, switches). Most of it ran on a scripted engine that returns prepared output, so the pairing, carry-over, release and publication logic could be checked against predictions written before the first push. A smaller phase used real engines (`stskill`, `claudecode`) and checked mechanics only. Real engines cost 12.38 USD.

**The core holds.** No scenario produced a second thread on GitHub, including an unfixed finding over five rounds and a finding that moved within the file. The release preview matches what is actually sent, byte for byte. Dry run, kill switch, shadow mode, rules with partner isolation, `/rereview`, repo discovery and retirement, and AI reply drafts all behave as the code says.

What did not hold is listed below, most severe first. Everything below is on master and none of it was caused by the aggregation. The typecheck break of #72 is left out on purpose: it is fixed in #72 itself.

## ❌ 1. The cross-round verifier never runs without an `active_provider` row

The verifier (`reconcile-findings.ts:817`), AI reply drafts (`reply-draft.ts:209`) and the cheap triage path read their provider from `engine_settings.active_provider`. Nothing writes that row: `setActiveProvider` has no caller anywhere in the code, the console never had one, and `SEED_ACTIVE_PROVIDER` is not read. Without the row the code falls back to `REVIEW_ENGINE`, which is an engine name (`claude-p`), not a profile. The profile does not resolve and the factory falls back to the boot engine with the global `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. That is empty when the token lives only on the profiles, so `claude -p` exits with "Not logged in". Reconcile swallows the error ("the verifier gave no usable answer"), and nothing is ever proposed as fixed.

The run showed it directly: a fixed XSS stayed a carried-over blocker for two rounds with "Nothing has proposed this finding as fixed". The 22 September drill only worked because `active_provider` had been set by hand in SQL.

**First step:** check production, `select * from engine_settings where key = 'active_provider';`. If the row is missing and the boot engine has no login of its own, every fresh deploy has this problem. Either way the fix belongs in code: a real writer, or a fallback to an enabled profile, plus a visible signal when the verifier fails instead of a silent "still open".

This is the verifier CZ3TDR1-662 delivers and the proposals CZ3TDR1-664's panel shows. Both tickets are closed; this item finishes them.

## ⚠️ 2. An unchanged finding gets a new thread when the engine flips its rule code

`stskill` reported the same unchanged finding as `F2` (catalog) in round 1, as a judgment without a code in round 2, and as `F2` again in round 3. `sameProblem` (`packages/github/src/draft.ts`) requires the same `ruleCode`, so round 2 opened a second thread. Master names this as a known cost of CZ3TDR1-725 ("duplicate mention, never a miss"). The new part is that it also happens with the calibrated skill engine, through a catalog ↔ judgment flip.

## ⚠️ 3. A released PR stays in the inbox as "In review · judge waiting"

On release only the judge row moves to `published` (`outbound-send.ts:713-731`). The engine rows stay `pending` until the next push, and `getPrInbox` (`apps/console/lib/queries.ts:205-210`) picks them up as a judge-less group. Every PR released in its first round ends up here, and the lane slowly fills with decided PRs.

## ⚠️ 4. The daily digest overstates pending reviews about tenfold

The digest (`apps/worker/src/index.ts:582-594`) counts every `pending` review row, without `provider = 'judge'` or `superseded_at IS NULL`. In the test DB it would have reported 115 reviews awaiting approval against 11 real ones, and the number grows with every round (same root as item 3).

## ⚠️ 5. The console requeue lock from #78 guards a path the console cannot reach

`requeueReviewAction` is only called from the `/ops` Re-run button, and only for a `rejected` row. No button can produce a `rejected` row (item 11). `failed` rows go through `rereviewPrAction` → `runRereview`, which does not take the lock. #78's description does not promise more, but the console race CZ3TDR1-739 was opened for stays open.

## ⚠️ 6. Re-run on a failed row of an old head leaves a permanent orphan in `/ops`

`runRereview` looks for `failed` rows on the live head only, and supersede skips `failed` rows on purpose (`reviews-write.ts:83-92`). A failed row from an older head therefore stays failed and un-superseded for ever. It shows in Needs attention without a SHA, and Re-run on it does nothing.

## ⚠️ 7. An engine revived after the judge stays outside the consensus

When one engine fails, the judge runs over a single draft. If Re-run then revives the other engine, its findings stay `draft` without curation, because `judgeReady` (`review-pr.ts:166`) refuses a second judge. The page still reports a finished consensus. Nothing leaks out, but a reviewer can miss the finding and the next push drops it.

## ⚠️ 8. The reason an engine failed is not visible anywhere in the console

The error text lives only in `review_events.meta` and the worker log. `/ops`, Activity and the worker step log read `action_logs` at level `error`, and `run-review.ts:415-425` writes nothing there. Without Slack a bare "failed" is the only signal that every engine failed.

## ⚠️ 9. A pending reply draft to the partner disappears on a newer round's page

An AI reply draft on a round-1 finding shows only on the round-1 page. `getPrReview` builds threads from the viewed round's findings only, and neither the inbox nor `/ops` signals it. When the next round comes back clean, the reviewer reaches the pending reply only through history.

## ⚠️ 10. The follow-up tells the partner "the code moved" when it is on the same line

A defect that returned to the same place (`src/render.js:9`) was taken as moved, because a move is detected from the anchor fingerprint, not from the line. The `finding_followup@v1` template assumes a different line (`outbound-templates.ts:80-82`). It is human-gated, but the reviewer has to notice that the text is wrong.

## ⚠️ 11. The console has no Reject and no Discard

`rejectAction` and `discardReviewAction` exist with correct guards, but no button calls them, on master or on #72. A reviewer cannot say "ignore this review". The only options are leaving it unreleased (it then sits in the inbox and the digest) or sending an empty release. This is also why item 5's lock cannot be reached.

## ⚠️ 12. `REVIEW_CONCURRENCY` holds its slots until the slowest review finishes

`boss.work(REVIEW_QUEUE, { batchSize }, … Promise.allSettled)` (`apps/worker/src/index.ts:438-469`) takes the next batch only after the whole batch is done. Together with a backlog, three rounds took 25–30 minutes from push instead of about 5.

## ⚠️ 13. The Partner filter in the inbox ignores the first interaction

Choosing a partner as the first action after the inbox loads changes neither the URL nor the result, and the select snaps back to "All". It reproduces every time. Repo and Claim work, and so does Partner after any other interaction. The cause in `startTransition` around `router.replace` is a guess.

## ⚠️ 14. Local `docker-compose.yml` does not pass `PROVIDER_*` to the console

Locally, `/admin/settings` shows "No provider profiles configured" and no engine or judge can be enabled. The VM compose gives the console `env_file: .env`, and the local one does not.

## 💡 Smaller things

- The "publishing live" chip does not hide on mobile (`Chip` concatenates classes without tailwind-merge), so every page overflows by 60 px at 390 px.
- The header shows the `publishEnabled` summary, not the kill switch. With the kill switch off it still said "publishing live · 1 partner".
- Policy-matrix selects, the outbound log filter and the judge select have no accessible name. Three toggles on Outbound share "turn off/turn on".
- The carried-over panel shows the findings of a just-released first round as "carried over · still open".
- A finding dropped by a human is binned under "Dropped by orchestrator".
- `resolved_evidence` on a canonical covering two rows at one place holds the hunk and reason twice (`reconcile-findings.ts:2310`).
- Threads and the daily sweep skip a PR with no open published finding left. Nothing reads that value today.
- A dismissed assistant error leaves the orphaned question in every later prompt's history.
- `outbound_messages.attempts` counts sends only, so the log cannot tell "held by the kill switch" from "stuck".
- The partner detail page (new in #72) shows publish as a badge with no toggle, and the list toggle is named only by `title`.
- The console allows watching a repo the bot cannot access, and discovery unwatches it within a poll.
- Enabling an engine backfills paid reviews onto the current head of every open PR in watched repos (intended, `triage.ts`). The confirm button mentions neither the backlog nor the cost.
- A fenced "/rereview" from a partner produces an AI reply draft. It waits for approval, so it is only noise.
- Unverified: a stale `command_ack` ("no new commit since …") left pending could be approved after the next round with an untrue text.

## Not covered by the run

- The real verifier itself (blocked by item 1). Worth repeating one real-engine fix round once item 1 is fixed.
- The carried-over panel with a bot that may comment but not resolve threads (all test repos gave the bot write access).
- The daily thread sweep as the trigger, rather than the Threads button.
- The derive branch and atomicity of the publication backfill (#79). Every release in the test DB was sent by current code, so only unit tests cover it.
- A precise requeue-vs-poll race (two of three attempts did not overlap), kill switch after exhausted retries, `/rereview` on a fresh head, and a denied command from a stranger.

**Done when:** item 1 is fixed and verified with one real-engine round in which a fixed finding is proposed as fixed, and every other item here is either fixed or moved to its own ticket with a decision.

Evidence: test PRs under `github.com/roman-talas-snowly-code/st-addon-drill-*` (branches `e2e-*`, left open). The full run report is kept locally by Roman.
